note: Choose a trail T with the maximum number of edges; existence follows because G has finitely many edges, every trail uses each edge at most once, and at least one one-edge trail exists. If its endpoints differ, the used-edge subgraph has odd degree at the terminal endpoint, while longestness means every incident edge is used, contradicting even degree in G. Once T is closed, any omitted edge can be connected to the trail vertex set; an omitted edge incident with that set exists. Rotate T to that endpoint and append the omitted edge, contradicting maximal length. This proves the target without external facts.
